title: Past Continuous
tagline: an action in progress at a past time
why: The past continuous sets the scene in a story: what was happening when something else happened. Without it, your stories sound like a list of facts.
understand: the difference between a longer background action (I was cooking) and a short action that interrupts it (the phone rang)
why What were you doing at 8? and What did you do at 8? mean different things
able: describe the background to a story: the weather, what people were doing
tell what you were doing when something happened
mistakes: We was watching TV when you called.
We were watching TV when you called.
When the phone rang, I cooked dinner.
When the phone rang, I was cooking dinner.
While I was walking home, I was seeing an accident.
While I was walking home, I saw an accident.
What you were doing at nine o'clock?
What were you doing at nine o'clock?
use: an action in progress at a past time: At 7 p.m. I was driving home.
a longer action interrupted by a short one (past simple): I was cooking when the power went out.
the background to a story: It was raining and people were hurrying to work.
two actions happening at the same time: While I was working, the kids were playing.
form: I / he / she / it was working. You / we / they were working.
signals: when, while, as, at 8 o'clock last night, at that moment, all day yesterday
tip: Think of a film: the past continuous is the long scene in the background (I was walking), and the past simple is the short event that happens in it (I saw a fox). Use while with the long action and when usually with the short one.

pick.q: I ___ a shower when the doorbell rang.
pick.why: The shower was the longer action in progress when the bell interrupted it: was having.

pick.q: At ten o'clock last night we ___ a movie.
pick.why: An action in progress at a past time uses the past continuous. With we, use were: were watching.

pick.q: While she was driving to work, she ___ a deer on the road.
pick.why: Seeing the deer is a short action that happened during the drive, so we use the past simple: saw.

pick.q: It ___ heavily when we left the restaurant.
pick.why: The snow is the background in progress, so we use was snowing (it takes was).

pick.q: They ___ to the radio, so they didn't hear us knock.
pick.why: They were in the middle of listening when we knocked: were listening (they takes were).

pick.q: What ___ you doing when the lights went out?
pick.why: Past continuous question: were + you + -ing. What were you doing?

pick.q: I ___ the answer, so I put up my hand.
pick.why: Know is a state verb and doesn't usually take -ing: I knew.

pick.q: He cut his finger while he ___ vegetables.
pick.why: After while we use the longer action in progress. He takes was: was chopping.

type.why: He was in the middle of sleeping when I called: was sleeping.

type.q: We ___ (not / pay) attention, so we missed our stop.
type.why: Negative past continuous with we: weren't + -ing. We weren't paying attention.

type.q: The sun ___ (shine) and the birds were singing.
type.why: This is the background of a scene, so we use the past continuous: was shining.

type.q: ___ (you / work) late last night when I texted?
type.why: Past continuous question: Were + you + -ing. Were you working?

type.q: At midnight my neighbours ___ (have) a loud party, so I couldn't sleep.
type.why: The party was in progress at that time. Neighbours is plural: were having.

type.q: I ___ (not / feel) well, so I stayed home.
type.why: Both are fine here: I wasn't feeling well (in progress) or I didn't feel well.

type.q: While the kids ___ (play) outside, it suddenly started to rain.
type.why: After while we use the longer action in progress: were playing.

type.q: She ___ (wait) for the bus when it started to rain.
type.why: She was in the middle of waiting when the rain started: was waiting.

spot.q: I was knowing his name but I forgot it.
spot.why: Know is a state verb, so we don't use -ing: I knew his name.

spot.q: We was talking about you this morning.
spot.why: With we, the past continuous uses were: We were talking.

spot.q: When the alarm went off, I slept deeply.
spot.why: Sleeping was in progress when the alarm interrupted it: I was sleeping.

spot.q: While I was shopping, I was meeting my old teacher.
spot.why: Meeting someone is a short event during the shopping, so we use the past simple: I met.

spot.q: What you were doing at midnight?
spot.why: In questions, were goes before the subject: What were you doing?

order.a: What were you doing at six o'clock?
order.why: Question word + were + subject + -ing: What were you doing?

order.a: I was making coffee when she arrived.
alt: When she arrived I was making coffee.
order.why: Long action (was making) + when + short action (arrived).

order.a: They weren't wearing their seat belts.
He fell asleep while he was reading.
alt: While he was reading he fell asleep.
order.why: Short action (fell asleep) + while + longer action (was reading).

pick.q: I ___ dinner when my sister called, so I didn't answer.
pick.why: Making dinner was in progress when the call came: was making.

pick.q: At noon yesterday they ___ lunch in the park.
pick.why: An action in progress at a past time. With they, use were: were eating.

pick.q: While we were jogging, it suddenly ___ to rain.
pick.why: 'Suddenly' shows a short event, so we use the past simple: started.

pick.q: She ___ a red dress at the wedding.
pick.why: We describe what someone was wearing at a past event with was + -ing (she takes was).

pick.q: ___ it raining when you left the house?
pick.why: Past continuous question with it: Was it raining?

pick.q: He ___ that car for ten years before he sold it.
pick.why: Own is a state verb and doesn't usually take -ing: he owned.

type.q: When the boss came in, everyone ___ (work) hard.
type.why: Everyone takes a singular verb: everyone was working.

type.q: I ___ (not / listen), so can you say that again?
type.why: Negative past continuous with I: wasn't + -ing.

type.q: The children ___ (laugh) at the clown when the lights went out.
type.why: Laughing was in progress when the lights went out. Children is plural: were laughing.

type.q: Why ___ (you / cry) when I saw you yesterday?
type.why: Past continuous question: Why + were + you + -ing.

type.q: My husband ___ (fix) the sink when he hurt his back.
type.why: Fixing the sink was the longer action that was interrupted: was fixing.

type.q: We ___ (drive) through the mountains when the car broke down.
type.why: Driving was in progress when the car broke down: were driving.

type.q: While I ___ (wait) at the doctor's, my phone rang.
type.why: After while we use the longer action in progress: was waiting.

type.q: The students ___ (not / talk) when the teacher came back.
type.why: Negative past continuous with a plural subject: weren't + -ing.

spot.q: She were cooking when I got home.
spot.why: With she, the past continuous uses was: She was cooking.

spot.q: I was wanting to call you but I was too busy.
spot.why: Want is a state verb, so we don't use -ing: I wanted to call you.

spot.q: The phone rang while I had a bath.
spot.why: After while we need the longer action in progress: while I was having a bath.

spot.q: While we were watching the game, our team was scoring a goal.
spot.why: A goal is a short event during the longer action, so we use the past simple: our team scored.

order.a: Were you sleeping when I phoned?
order.why: Past continuous question: Were + subject + -ing + when + past simple.

order.a: It was getting dark when we got home.
alt: When we got home it was getting dark.
order.why: Background (was getting dark) + when + short action (got home).

order.a: I wasn't looking at the screen.

bank.q: I ___ along the lake when I saw the fireworks.
bank.why: Walking was in progress when I saw the fireworks: was walking (I takes was).

bank.q: At 3 p.m. yesterday we ___ in a meeting.
bank.why: An action in progress at a past time: were sitting.

bank.q: While he was cleaning the garage, he ___ an old photo.
bank.why: Finding the photo is a short event during the cleaning, so we use the past simple: found.

bank.q: What ___ she doing when you arrived?
bank.why: Past continuous question with she: What was she doing?

bank.q: I ___ you were in Vancouver last week.
bank.why: Know is a state verb and doesn't take -ing: I didn't know.

bank.q: The kids ___ TV, so they didn't hear the phone.
bank.why: The kids were in the middle of watching TV. Kids is plural: were watching.

bank.q: When I heard the news, I ___ my mother right away.
bank.why: First I heard the news, then I called. Two short actions in order both use the past simple: called.

bank.q: She ___ on the phone all through dinner.
bank.why: An action in progress over a past period with she: was talking.

bank.q: I ___ (read) in bed when I heard a strange noise.
bank.why: Reading was in progress when I heard the noise: was reading.

bank.q: They ___ (not / wear) coats when I saw them, and it was freezing!
bank.why: Negative past continuous with they: weren't + -ing.

bank.q: ___ (he / drive) too fast when the police stopped him?
bank.why: Past continuous question: Was + he + -ing.

bank.q: While we ___ (have) lunch, a bird flew into the window.
bank.why: After while we use the longer action in progress: were having.

bank.q: The wind ___ (blow) and the rain was falling hard.
bank.why: Background to a scene uses the past continuous: was blowing.

bank.q: They was waiting outside for an hour.
bank.why: With they, the past continuous uses were: They were waiting.

bank.q: I was believing every word he said.
bank.why: Believe is a state verb, so we don't use -ing: I believed.

bank.q: We were having breakfast when the power went out.
bank.why: This sentence is correct: the longer action (were having) was interrupted by a short one (went out).

bank.q: When I saw her, she talked on her phone.
bank.why: She was in the middle of a phone call when I saw her: she was talking.

bank.a: What were they talking about yesterday?
bank.why: Question word + were + subject + -ing + about.

bank.a: I was driving home when it happened.
alt: When it happened I was driving home.
bank.why: Long action (was driving) + when + short action (happened).

bank.a: She wasn't feeling well that morning.
alt: That morning she wasn't feeling well.
bank.why: Negative past continuous: subject + wasn't + -ing.
